video_title: Kevin Garnett on his HONEST THOUGHTS about the MVP or Championship conversation 👀

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Randolph asks Kevin Garnett about valuing MVP versus championship awards
quotes.excerpt: Does it mean the most to you to have the MVP over the championship?

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: Before you get out of here, I want to know, you get both awards. Well, team award and individual award. I want to know, does it mean the most to you to have the MVP over the championship? Or would you rather just have the championship and not the MVP? Which one would you have to prefer if Kevin Garnett wasn't fortunate enough to get both?

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Garnett
text_blocks.text: So your patches and your stripes to make you up who you are is what they going to remember you by. When you get them awards and them all-star and shit, those are what you earned in the thing. When you get that Larry O'Brien, you're in the guys. Y'all came together for one goal and got this. Not one person did any of this. Coaches went into this, equipment manager, everybody went into the Larry O'Brien. When you get that one joint, yeah, you need teammates to get it there. You got to put in the basket, you got to perform, you got to be that consistently. But them stripes and what you get, bro, them just stripes, them them patches. They going to know who you are, bro. They going to know Big G, they going to know Big Five, they going to know. And that's that's what those are. When you get them individual awards, bro, those are your badges. Those are no different from the scar you got on your face, from your finger being fucked up, your knee. What you put into this game and your badges and what you're collecting in it ain't no different from them war marks that's on your arm.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Garnett
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Garnett prefers winning an NBA championship over individual accolades
quotes.excerpt: Yeah, give me the championship all day.
quotes.quote: Yeah, give me the championship all day. They going to know me anyway for these stripes and these battle wounds, but yeah, what we did with the guys, yeah, that's between us and the guys. That can never be emulated.

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Randolph reflects on the preparation required for NBA success
quotes.excerpt: I dove into just the preparation and how you came in the locker room.
quotes.quote: Speaking of individual, top 75, I thought that was a huge award. When you actually got selected, for me, I dove into just the preparation and how you came in the locker room. You demanded the attention, respect, and a work ethic that was so contagious amongst the locker room. You used to come in and work out with the young fellas, having us on point, hitting that iron. Those sumo squats, I'll never forget the sumo squats. You love the damn sumo squats. But I'm talking about that hard work and when we wanted it, you was anything possible. And if anybody don't know how hard you work, bro, it was an honor to be able to steal a page out of your book, take that to Memphis, and bro, you get your flowers on Out the Mud.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Garnett
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Garnett recalls his motivational tactics in the locker room
quotes.excerpt: You just got to have grit and balls, baby.
quotes.quote: He used to come in the locker room, we'd get a big win, we'd win, we probably look like we about to lose, he'd come in late after the interview, 'You just got to have grit and balls, baby. Just grit and balls up in here, baby.' So you remember? Yeah, I already know he's checking, he's checking the blueprint. We used to come in here, hey man, this is the same drill. Hey, grit and balls on three, one, two, three, grit and balls. Like I'll put my hand on that, but I'll go grit and balls. You know that. The meaning in behind it, bro, we'd be down 20, 25, talking about comeback games. I'm talking about real gritty, bro. I'm talking about just like how we used to. We going to walk them down.
